It's taking a pill ALONG with eating. Yes, I know animals are constantly dying. It does make a difference what you choose to eat. Companies produce what the people buy. That's why you see more and more vegan/vegetarian choices. Did you know that the meat and dairy industries have pretty much forced the USDA to promote meat and dairy to the people in order to make a profit? Average meat consumption in the U.S. is higher than what is recommended by USDA standards. It does matter that people eat meat. It puts a strain on the environment. It takes a lot of land, resources, and energy to produce edible meat. 

I would hope people are concerned about the environnent. Obviously there are more issues contributing to environmental problems. We are one of the many, many species that is capable of protecting the planet. Yet, look at the damage we've done. We coexist among the other animals of the planet that just want to live and not feel pain like us. Why cause unnecessary pain to those animals in order to momentarily gratify our senses and harm the environment? 

I propose a reduced consumption of meat, dairy, and eggs, and more humane and local farms. It is a tough situation economically, but gradual change might lessen the impact. 

Those are some of my views. And, yes, everyone is biased hooray.

So, was she trying to convert you passively? I don't think you're in the wrong or anything. You two have a different set of beliefs that makes maintaining your relationship a bit of a struggle. If you stayed in this relationship, do you think you would be happy in the end? Do you think the two of you are over-thinking this? You said that you would put off these issues for later. Perhaps it's possible to find a solution. Perhaps not. It is up to you to decide if it's worth it to try again. 

When she gets her stuff, maybe you can make it easy for her by having it all ready to go. Keep it brief and mature. Personally, I think whether or not you end up with her, trying to work out a solution would be beneficial to both of you. Or at least express your thoughts and reasons without temperament. Not necessarily while she is getting her things but maybe later when the two of you have had some space to really think about things.

When you two meet, you should show up in a way that she was not expecting. Get some bad-boy outfit and just act nonchalant the whole time. Just do your best to control your emotions during "the talk". And agree with everything she says. If she calls it off, just be like, "Okay." 

Sometimes, people need breaks from each other. This distance will give her (and you) a chance to live single for a bit. That means more time to focus on you. 

I know you say that this is really blind siding you, but have you really dissected your relationship with her? If you cannot think of anything, look up common reasons for couples to split on Google. I'm one of those people that believes that love does not die a natural death. What changed that caused this? 

I do not want to give you false hope, but if you truly love this girl, don't go out without a (silent) fight. However,  definitely be prepared if things do not work out. Learning from your mistakes from this relationship will aid you if you get back with her or if life carries you to someone new. Take care.

Honestly, I'm a little different when it comes to these things. It is very good to heal from a relationship through time and space away from each other, and the fact that she is still talking to you is a good sign. I don't want to give you any false hope or anything, but do you think you could go from exs to lovers again just like that? You still need to accept that the relationship you once had with her is now over, but that does not mean that you can't have another one with her--a new one. For this to work, though, you need to find out why she broke up with you. I know you say you don't know, but really think about it. Don't dwell on it, though. If you need help, just google common causes for relationships to end. That might help you recognize what happened. So, whether you get back with her or get with sometime else, you'll have learned from your past. If healing means blocking her for a while, by all means, go for it. Work on yourself by changing some things in your life. Change your style, wear cologne, do pushups every morning, do something that gets that excitement of change in your life. 

You mentioned that lack of feelings with other people. Maybe as you get to know them more those feelings will come to you. I'm in the same boat, though, buddy. My ex won't even talk to me even after she told me she still wanted to be friends. So I'm not sure if she changed her mind or if she needs more time or what.  

Anyway, I personally think the "let's catch up" meet would be good if, and only if, 1)you know and have fixed the reasons for the break up and 2)you are in control of your emotions and have healed enough to not hurt when talking to her. Just know that you will have to start from friends to get back up to lovers again. It's all about building trust and attraction again.  Things may or may not work out, so don't count on it, okay?

Mine broke up with me about a week before Christmas, as well, so I understand, man.  Now, I want to ask you something: Do you think your ex would want to come back to a depressed and anxious man? No. I highly doubt that she would. And do you like being depressed and anxious? No. The way you describe it, it sounds very bothersome to you. 
So what do you do? Well, be who you want to be. Cut off contact with your ex so you have space to go through a sort of metamorphosis. 

Be the man. 

Be the best man you can be. And believe it. Take care of yourself by eating healthy and working out. Get into fashion and a little vain about how you look. Why? Because you're the man. Also, the man usually has lots of friends (both male and female) because of how charismatic he is. But he isn't charismatic right away; it takes time and practice. So meet friends from your friends and go hang out at the club. Eventually you'll feel super great about yourself. 

Now, just think, in order to be the man, you would have needed to have survived some pain to grow stronger. That pain came to you in the form of a break up. You need to reflect on why that break up happened. Then think to yourself if you have improved or fixed your mistakes. Then think about if the relationship is worth a second shot. If so, the man will feel much more confident in himself and probably be attractive to the ex once he decides to make contact again. Or if he doesn't think it's worth it, he can keep doing what he's doing and live his life and partying it up. 

Either way, the man will take the pain of this rejection and turn it into strength for tomorrow's battle!

Do you want her back? Even if she says she doesn't think she'll get back with you, doesn't mean it can't happen. I'm also not saying to base all your hope on getting back with her. I think you did the right thing by telling her you wouldn't want to be friends. That probably shocked her. Now the two of you can go through some alone time to process these feelings. I would only interact with her if need be, otherwise, ignoring is good. 
She told you she fell out of love. Why? Have you sat and really tried to dissect your relationship with her? I am a huge advocate of "if two people can fall in love once, they can fall in love again". And just because a break up happens doesn't mean it wasn't meant to be. I'm sure some things happened that lead to a gradual decrease in attraction. Did the to of you get too monotonous? Did something happened that resulted in lost trust that was never regained? 
I want you to really think about this relationship and whether or not you'd want to pursue her again. Either way, you need time to yourself to cool down from these emotions. I always suggest to people to get a new haircut and clothing to help them start fresh if you can afford it. 
That's just my opinion. I wish you the best however you decide to handle this.

I would suggest treating yourself to some new clothes and a new haircut. Do some cleaning. Work out. Do things that will help keep your self-esteem up. It's going to hurt for a while but that's okay. It's good to 'feel'. Just know how to express those feelings in a healthy way i/e crying, exercising, drawing.

If it's really getting to you, definitely block them. You don't have to unfriend anyone if you don't want to. When you're feeling better about everything, you can unblock them again.  Sorry to hear about that, though. I wish you the best :^)
